title: Naked Business: Why radical honesty in marketing and sales makes bootstrappers more money
summary: Jason Cohen argues that proactive honesty (admitting weaknesses, being small, showing negatives) is a competitive differentiator that raises sales, cuts returns and churn, and builds believability. He backs it with Canon review data, his hosting outage cancellation data, Balsamiq's one-person About page, and enterprise sales stories.

principles.text: Showing negatives alongside positives lifts sales and profit, because buyers who know the trade-offs decide sooner.
principles.quote: it is a universal rule that if you say the good and the bad you sell more and you make more profit

principles.text: Honest expectations cut returns, and returns are very expensive relative to thin margins.
principles.quote: returns of the products went down 20% and the returns went down for the same reason because I know the door opens then I don't return it

principles.text: Be proactively honest, not just honest when asked. Admitting flaws earns the credibility to make positive claims believed.
principles.quote: when you admit the problems or admit things that could be a negative you you earn the ability to then say happy things and people believe you

principles.text: During outages, communicate immediately and openly; proactive updates can fully offset the churn silence would cause.
principles.quote: because we proactively talked about every problem as it came out it mitigated a hundred percent of people's negative opinion about what was going on

principles.text: Don't hide being small. A customer who rejects you for it would have been unhappy anyway, and pretending sours the relationship.
principles.quote: they don't want to work with you because you're too small and if you try to pretend like you're not too small Lockheed Martin's going to find out

principles.text: Lean into the advantages only a small company has: take on risk, move faster, be all-in on the customer, and say so plainly.
principles.quote: these are your competitive advantages you don't have many these are what they are so you must bang them on the head and use them
